blockers: Line 148-151 in qttunebridge.cpp: Signal decoding hardcoded to 8-byte CAN while qttune_frame_t.data[64] is clearly CAN-FD sized (64 bytes). The decode call `qttune_decode_signal(&def, frame->data, 8, &val)` ignores the actual frame data_length field and uses wrong buffer size.

Lines 114-116 in qttunebridge.h: SignalListModel class completely removed from header but references still exist in comments and code - indicates incomplete refactoring or dead code that was never properly migrated.
Lines 51-55 in Main.qml: UI references QtTune.signalModel which no longer exists in bridge after diff - creates dangling QML binding to removed property.

Lines 149-160 in qttunebridge.cpp: Removed code shows signal decoding was done per-frame in handleFrameInternal with batching timer. This entire signal pipeline has been deleted, breaking signal display functionality entirely.
Line 47-49 in qttunebridge.h: SignalListModel* m_signalModel member removed but onFrame callback signature unchanged - potential null pointer dereference if code tries to use it.
questions: What is the intended behavior for signal display? The LiveViewPage.qml showing signal values has been completely deleted, yet the QML Main.qml still references QtTune.connected and signalModel properties that no longer exist.
Is the 64-byte CAN-FD buffer in qttune_frame_t intentional? If so, why was signal decoding hardcoded to 8 bytes? This mismatch suggests either a bug or incomplete migration.
What happened to the signal batching/coalescing logic that was being developed? The tests for signal batches were removed but the feature appears to be completely eliminated rather than refactored.
Is there a separate signal handling implementation elsewhere that should be used instead of the deleted code?
The comment on line 117 in qttunebridge.h mentions 'QAtomicInteger<int> m_notifyRateCounter{0}; for rate calc (optional, per-second)' but this is commented out - is this intentional?
nits: Line 60 in qttunebridge.cpp: Comment 'back-eviction at capacity' should clarify that eviction is FIFO (oldest first) since frames are appended to back and evicted from front.
Line 87 in qttunebridge.h: Comment about 'Rows NEVER reorder' should note that FrameSortProxy handles the actual sorting, making the storage layer a simple FIFO.
Line 138 in qttunebridge.cpp: Comment 'frame is stack-owned by mock_worker' assumes knowledge not visible in this diff - should document lifetime guarantees.
Removed code had good comments explaining the coalescing batching design (100ms window) - these design decisions should be preserved or clarified.
